identity.question: Reserve Bank of Australia increases interest rates by 50+ bps at the November 2026 meeting?

rule: Cash rate target change resulting from the RBA Monetary Policy Board November 2–3 2026 meeting relative to the level prior to the meeting; source official RBA information including the November statement/release. If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound. If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). Displayed options of "Increase" or "Decrease" will include policy rate increases or decreases of any size. If the specified meeting is postponed to a date and time before the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve based on the outcome of that postponed meeting. If the specified meeting is cancelled, or postponed such that no decision is announced by the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No Change" bracket. Emergency changes to the specified rate not resulting from the specified meeting will not be considered.

facts.last_decision: 29 Sep 2026: +25bp to 4.60%, effective 30 Sep. RBA cited elevated inflation, upside risks materializing, higher global energy prices and AI-related prices, domestic capacity pressure, firm cost/pricing pressures, and inflation stronger than expected at previous meeting. Output growth slowed but June quarter stronger than expected; housing prices/new loans declined; labour conditions eased broadly as expected.
facts.minutes: Published 13 Oct 2026. Members unanimously raised 25bp; inflation remained too high and August upside risks materialized/built. Minutes say further increase remains possible if required.
facts.meeting_clock: RBA calendar: Monetary Policy Board Nov 2–3, then Dec 7–8. Cash-rate page says next update 2:30pm Sydney time Nov 3 and that decisions/target are published 2:30pm after each Board meeting.
facts.cpi: Latest ABS at capture: Aug 2026 CPI, released 30 Sep 11:30am AEST: headline +4.0% y/y vs +3.5% July; trimmed mean +3.6% unchanged; monthly CPI +0.4% original, +0.7% seasonally adjusted. Sept CPI scheduled 28 Oct 11:30am AEDT, before RBA meeting; quarterly CPI tables updated with Sep monthly publication.
facts.labor: Latest ABS: Sep 2026 Labour Force, released 15 Oct 11:30am AEDT: SA unemployment 4.7% (+0.1ppt), employment −39,300 (−0.3%) to 14,782,700, participation 66.8%; trend unemployment 4.6% unchanged. October labor release scheduled 19 Nov 11:30am AEDT, after RBA decision.
